cost: HE LANDS 93, THE TOP EDGE OF 90 +-3, AND 93 IS THE FLOOR OF WHAT IS REACHABLE WITHOUT TOUCHING THE DEADEYE VALUE. With both lifts switched off entirely the subject still reads the cap, 0.95 -> out 94 -> 3pt 93, because his deadeye value (0.88 x acc .994 + 0.12 x vol .835 = 0.975) is over the cap by construction. 90 is reachable only by lowering EYE_CAP itself or by discounting the accuracy read (a count ramp on the deadeye PATH prints 92 and breaks Richard Hamilton '06). A later round that wants 90 is arguing with the cap's value or with ERA_ALPHA, not with the lifts.

THE LOAD SHARE — the other half of his ruling — WAS MEASURED FIRST AND BREAKS FIVE OFF ANCHORS. recal_145's shape on this term's own class (recal_96's 12-minute foot; of the 1,850 cards the premium pays, vol > 0.70 and mp >= 1200, the p75 of mpg is 33.87) reaches the SAME 93 for the subject on a quarter of the collateral, and fails: Malik Beasley '23 off 58 -> 51 and Buddy Hield '25 58 -> 53 (both r137), Anthony Tolliver '14 (r99), Donyell Marshall '07 and Matt Bullard '92 (both r170). Those five rulings say a low-minute shooter IS his shooting, so minutes cannot price a three-point lift. The count ramp asks the different question — how many shots is this bar standing on — and holds all 193.

THE COST THE COUNT RAMP DOES PAY, NAMED. 4,133 of 10,000 bars fall, but 3,566 of them by one point and nearly all in the teens, where a non-shooter's bar lives: the boost is 8% of a composite that for a man who does not shoot is mostly a free-throw stand-in. OFF moves on 371 cards (350 of them by one), OVR on 195, DEF on zero. Five named cards move an OVR on a 1-point bar they do not use, and three of those move UP because compute_ovr's zone block re-sorts z[0..2] when the third zone drops: Chris Webber '95 78 -> 80, Dwyane Wade '06 89 -> 90, Patrick Ewing '87 76 -> 77, against Magic Johnson '83 87 -> 86 and Yao Ming '07 87 -> 86. That machinery is compute_ovr's, not this file's; a lane that wants it flat should look at the zone sort, not at the 3pt bar.

NO CARD RISES A POINT OF 3pt. Both lifts are scaled by a ramp <= 1 and the cap only subtracts, so the term is monotone non-increasing over the whole pool — the top 12 is name-for-name identical and every card with a full season's threes behind it is byte-identical.

THE ROUND KEPT ITS TERM INSIDE THE 3PT COMPOSITE. Nothing in perdef, ballsec or the mid composite is touched (rounds 195/197/199/201 are live in those terms); o_ovr / d_ovr / ovr follow from the attribute and compute_ovr is unchanged apart from its PIPELINE_VERSION stamp.
notes: THE SUBJECT, DECOMPOSED FROM data/provenance.json BEFORE ANYTHING WAS TOUCHED. Jim Les '91: 3pt path 1 (deadeye), 5.6 3PA/100, era multiplier 1.6938, .461, vol .835, acc .994, chucker gate 1.000. gunner composite 0.65 x .835 + 0.35 x .994 = 0.891; deadeye value 0.88 x .994 + 0.12 x .835 = 0.975, CAPPED to 0.95; the volume premium +0.07 x (.835-.70)/.30 = +0.0315 added AFTER the cap -> 0.9815 -> out 97 -> (97/99)^1.12 -> 3pt 97. Underneath it the gunner boost paid 0.891 x 1.08 = 0.9619 on its own, which is card 95 — so re-applying the cap alone reaches 95, not the 93 the scout expected, and the boost is what the round had to reach.

WHY THE BOOST IS THE SAME OBJECT AS THE PREMIUM. The de-stack round made them exclusive in this file's own words — 'the gunner boost and the volume premium are alternatives', max of the two, never both — so they are two prices for one claim: that this man shot a high volume of threes. One of them was gated (vol > 0.70) and neither was ever asked how many shots stood behind it. recal_51 wrote the objection ('attempts are a RATE, per hundred'), recal_78 built the answer for the rim and mid deadeye floors, recal_126 extended it to the diet, recal_145 put the mid premium on a load share and recal_166 put the paint premium on the discounted rate. The 3PT lifts are the last two terms in the file that never heard any of it.

THE CAP RE-APPLICATION IS CONTINUOUS AND THE OBVIOUS FORM IS NOT. A naive min(OUT, EYE_CAP) whenever the deadeye path wins was measured and rejected: a card at vol = acc = 0.95 sits exactly on the eye == gun crossing, and a ten-thousandth of accuracy would drop it 99 -> 93. Paying the premium to each path BEFORE comparing them — max(min(1, gun + prem), min(EYE_CAP, eye + prem)) — is continuous at the crossing, can never fall below what the gunner path already earned, and is byte-identical for every card whose deadeye value plus premium stays under the cap.

MEASURED ON THE WHOLE POOL BEFORE APPLYING. 3pt: 4,133 movers, ALL DOWN, distribution -1 x 3,566, -2 x 543, -3 x 19, -4 x 5. The subject's rank on the 3pt board goes 71st -> 184th of 10,000. Every pin the dispatch named was read before and after: Hamilton '06 60/60, Kerr '96 61/61, Korver '15 58/58, Hield '25 58/58, Beasley '23 56/56, Snell '18 50/50, Bowen '06 45/45, Curry '16 96/96, Miller '97 87/87, Seth Curry '23 mid 95/95. 193 anchors, 0 failing, mean |error| 0.83 — identical to the reading at 188.

THE CLASS THE ROUND FOUND IS ONE ARCHETYPE AND IT READS LIKE IT: thin-sample specialists whose bar was built on a part-season of threes — Bobby Simmons '09 86 -> 82, Michael Redd '02 and Michael Porter Jr. '21 98 -> 94, Seth Curry '20 and Luke Kennard '23 96 -> 93, Danny Green '12 97 -> 94, Pat Garrity '01 95 -> 92, Ben Gordon '06 95 -> 92, and from the other end of the file Dale Ellis '85 78 -> 74 and Craig Hodges '86 85 -> 82. Every deadeye with a full season behind him — Curry, Korver '15, Klay '15, Duncan Robinson '20, Ray Allen '06, Hield, Beasley — does not move a point.
